newsitem.title: CONGO: Bursts of gunfire at Congo army HQ panic city.
newsitem.headline: Bursts of gunfire at Congo army HQ panic city.

text.p: Sustained bursts of automatic weapons fire at Congo's army headquarters on Monday created panic in the commercial centre of the capital Brazzaville, witnesses said.
Armoured vehicles moved out from the camp into the centre of the city only three km (two miles) from Kinshasa, the capital of war-torn Zaire, across the Zaire river.
Passers-by fled and many civil servants left work early while some shopkeepers closed their businesses.
A military source who refused to be identified said soldiers were protesting against the government for abandoning a proposed law that would have improved living and working conditions for the army.
There were no immediate reports of casualties.
After the shooting ended armed forces Chief of Staff General Daniel Mabika left his office to meet the government in search of a solution to the dispute, the source said.
Fighting among politically and ethnically based militias loyal to Congo's political rivals after disputed legislative elections in 1993 killed an estimated 2,000 people in Brazzaville's suburbs.
Anticipating trouble across the river in Kinshasa, troops from the United States, Belgium, France and Britain are based in Brazzaville to evacuate Western nationals from Zaire if the need arises.
